items.title: Every function is operable with the keyboard alone, without timing requirements, and character-key shortcuts can be turned off or remapped.
items.guidance: Unplug the mouse. Reach and operate every control with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys and Escape. Check custom widgets against the ARIA Authoring Practices keyboard patterns.
items.notes: Open with Enter/Space, Tab cycles Cancel/Delete, Escape closes. Also covered by InteractiveComponentTests.

items.title: Focus order is logical and preserves meaning; focus moves into and out of overlays as expected and returns to the trigger on close.
items.guidance: Tab through the UI and compare the order with the visual reading order. Open and close dialogs, menus and popovers and confirm where focus goes.
items.notes: Focus moves to Cancel on open and returns to the trigger on close.

items.title: A visible focus indicator is present on every focusable element and is not hidden behind sticky headers, footers or overlays.
items.guidance: Tab through the UI at 100% and 200% zoom, in light and dark themes and with Windows high contrast / forced colors.

items.title: Link and control names describe their purpose, headings and labels are descriptive, and visible label text is part of the accessible name.
items.guidance: Review the accessible names (browser accessibility tree or a screen reader's elements list) against the visible labels.

items.title: Content works at 200% text zoom and reflows at 320 CSS pixels wide (400% zoom) without two-dimensional scrolling or loss of content.
items.guidance: Zoom to 400% at 1280px wide, and separately increase text size to 200%.

items.title: No content is clipped or overlaps when text spacing is increased (line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter spacing 0.12, word spacing 0.16).
items.guidance: Apply a text-spacing bookmarklet or user stylesheet and review every state.

items.title: Text and meaningful graphics meet contrast in every state (hover, focus, selected, disabled, error), including text over images or gradients that tools cannot measure.
items.guidance: Measure with a color picker where automated results were inconclusive; check focus indicators and icons against adjacent colors.

items.title: Information is not conveyed by color, shape, size or position alone.
items.guidance: Review status indicators, charts, required-field markers and error states in grayscale.

items.title: Errors are identified in text, associated with their fields, explained with suggestions, and important submissions can be reviewed or reversed.
items.guidance: Submit forms with missing and invalid data; confirm messages are visible, associated with fields and announced.

items.title: Labels and instructions are provided, and status messages (saved, loading, results count) are announced without moving focus.
items.guidance: Trigger each asynchronous operation with a screen reader running and confirm the announcement.

items.title: Tooltips and popovers that appear on hover or focus are dismissible (Escape), hoverable and persistent.
items.guidance: Hover and focus each trigger; press Escape; move the pointer onto the popup.

items.title: Nothing flashes more than three times per second, moving or auto-updating content can be paused, time limits can be extended, and animations respect reduced-motion preferences.
items.guidance: Review carousels, spinners, toasts and session timeouts; enable 'reduce motion' in the OS.

items.title: Path-based gestures and dragging have single-pointer alternatives, actions fire on pointer up, and targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or adequately spaced.
items.guidance: Operate sliders, sortable lists and drag-and-drop with a single click/tap alternative; check target sizes.
items.justification: The dialog has no dragging or path-based gestures; its buttons are 44px targets.

items.title: Representative screen reader testing confirms names, roles, states, reading order and announcements (for example NVDA + Firefox/Chrome, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari, TalkBack + Chrome).
items.guidance: Record which assistive technology and browser versions were used in Environments.
items.notes: Example entry: verify the dialog name and description are announced with NVDA + Firefox and VoiceOver + Safari before release.
